competencyFramework.name: Franklin's 9 Transdisciplinary Competencies
competencyFramework.description: Canonical definitions from Franklin's TD Competencies Rubric (2026). Used across grading, narratives, council reviews, and transition reports.

competencies.name: Collaboration
competencies.description: Works productively and respectfully with others to achieve shared goals

competencies.name: Storytelling / Communication
competencies.description: Communicates ideas clearly, creatively, and appropriately for audience and purpose

competencies.name: Reflexivity
competencies.description: Reflects critically on learning, decisions, and assumptions

competencies.name: Empathy / Perspective Taking
competencies.description: Demonstrates understanding and respect for others' perspectives and experiences

competencies.name: Knowledge-Based Reasoning
competencies.description: Applies disciplinary and interdisciplinary knowledge to solve problems

competencies.name: Futures Thinking
competencies.description: Envisions and prepares for multiple and preferred futures

competencies.name: Systems Thinking
competencies.description: Identifies and understands interconnections within and across systems

competencies.name: Adaptability
competencies.description: Responds constructively to change and ambiguity

competencies.name: Agency
competencies.description: Takes initiative and ownership of learning and actions

default.description: Franklin generic page layout — banner with course name + page title, school logo, course nav strip, then the freeform body. Used for any Canvas wiki page that doesn't fit the lesson/assessment/module_outcomes templates (exit tickets, short reflection pages, announcements, ad-hoc resources). Applied automatically when create_page is called without an explicit template.

module_outcomes.description: Franklin Module Outcomes page. Banner with course name + module title, school logo, course nav strip, and a single 'Outcomes' section with an ordered list of what students will be able to do by the end of the module.

outcomes.description: Ordered-list items (<li>) listing what students will be able to do by the end of the module. Each <li> is one observable outcome (start with an action verb: Design, Build, Evaluate, Analyze, Apply, etc.). Outcomes should be competency-aligned where possible — 4-8 items is typical.

about.description: What students will learn about (the topic / content). 1-2 sentence summary.

to.description: What skills students will gain — typically a short bulleted list of can-do statements.

concepts.description: Key concepts and terms with brief definitions.

resources.description: Links to readings, videos, websites, or other materials referenced in the lesson.

tasks.description: Tasks for students to complete during the lesson.

discussion.description: Discussion forum link or prompt. Only used when a discussion forum is part of the lesson.

assessment.description: Link to a related assessment task (when there is one).

discussion.description: Discussion forum accordion. Off by default — most lessons don't use one. Pass include_sections: ['discussion'] when the teacher mentions a discussion or debate.

assessment.description: Linked-assessment accordion. On by default — most lessons either have a related assessment or expect one will be added later. Pass omit_sections: ['assessment'] for purely formative lessons.

Franklin assessment page layout. Banner with course name + assessment title, school logo, course nav strip, then six required blocks: Assessment Description, Pre-Work, Structure and Grading (with grade boundaries table), Submission, Time, and Use of Artificial Intelligence.

description.description: Top-level description of what the assessment is. Typically an intro paragraph followed by a numbered or bulleted list of what students will do.

pre_work.description: What students should have completed BEFORE taking the assessment. Typically a short paragraph plus a numbered list of prerequisites.

structure_and_grading.description: Three things in one block: (1) a paragraph describing what students should expect (number of questions, points, etc.), (2) grade weighting (what percent of the trimester this assessment is worth), and (3) a grade boundaries table mapping letter grades A+ through F to point ranges. Generate the full HTML including a <table> with rows for A+, A, A-, B+, B, B-, C+, C, C-, D, and F.

submission.description: How students are expected to submit their work (in-class on paper, upload to Canvas, etc.).

time.description: Time allotment. Include both standard time and extended-time accommodations if relevant. For long-term projects, a timeline goes here.

ai_use.description: Acceptable and unacceptable uses of AI for this assessment. Typically two bulleted lists — one for each. Be explicit and assessment-specific (a writing assignment has different AI rules than a math test).
